artifacts.summary: 7-phase implementation closing the consumer-deploy-propagation gap by moving the existing per-extension freshness check to per-dispatch granularity inside skill_preflight_update and injecting a <deploy-freshness-context> block into the dispatch brief; both this repo and ~/Projects/BimodalLogic redeployed clean.

completion_data.completion_summary: Closed the consumer-deploy-propagation gap by re-firing the existing per-extension, path-scoped freshness comparison once per skill/agent dispatch (skill_preflight_update in skill-base.sh) and injecting the result into the generated dispatch file (orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh's <deploy-freshness-context> block), rather than building a new detector. Pinned partial-staleness detection with a fixture, measured the added per-dispatch cost (~106ms, ~435-1875x cheaper than the removed fleet walk), documented the decision and three rejected alternatives, and verified end-to-end by redeploying both this repo and ~/Projects/BimodalLogic (all four previously-cited lean call sites now confirmed byte-identical to source).

memory_candidates.content: When an existing detector fails to prevent the defect it detects, check its placement and granularity before concluding a new detector is needed. A pull-side, per-extension staleness check already existed and already fired non-blockingly, but only once per top-level command and only onto the orchestrating session's own stderr -- never into a spawned subagent's own context. The fix was to re-fire the SAME unchanged comparison at per-dispatch granularity and inject the result into the context the subagent actually reads (a generated dispatch file), not to build a new comparison mechanism. A test suite that resolves its subject-under-test from a deployed tree first (deployed-tree-first / source-store-fallback candidate resolution) will silently test STALE code if the source store was edited but not yet redeployed -- always redeploy before trusting such a suite's PASS after a source-store change, and confirm by diffing deployed against source directly rather than assuming a redeploy landed.

In a bash test fixture that overrides SKILL_REPO_ROOT to isolate a function call from the real repo, a bare `cd` into the fixture is NOT sufficient when the code under test reads $SKILL_REPO_ROOT directly (as opposed to a bare relative path resolved via cwd) -- SKILL_REPO_ROOT is typically exported once, process-wide, when the library was first sourced, and a later `cd` never updates it. Must explicitly prefix the call: `SKILL_REPO_ROOT="$FIXTURE_ROOT" some_function args...`. Omitting this silently falls through to checking the REAL repo's own state instead of the fixture's fabricated one -- a false pass if the real repo happens to be in the expected state, and a confusing false fail otherwise.
